CVE-2026-111729.description:
In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, the "Command" file-upload handler at `POST /admin/denali/file/command` extracts a client-supplied ZIP archive into the configured `command.working.directory`. The path-containment check `validateFileName()` compares canonical paths with `String.startsWith()` without appending a trailing path separator, so an entry that canonicalises to a sibling directory sharing the same string prefix (e.g. `/tmpevil/x` when the intended directory is `/tmp`) is accepted. The handler then calls `parent.mkdirs()` and `new FileOutputStream(newFile)`, creating directories and writing attacker-controlled bytes outside the intended extraction root.

The command service is disabled by default since Kura 4.0.0 [1]. The issue does not apply when the command service is disabled. The caller must be authenticated with `rest.command` permission.

CVE-2026-116131.title: HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl allow memory and temporary file exhaustion via an unlimited number of form fields and multipart parts
CVE-2026-116131.description:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl allow memory and temporary file exhaustion via an unlimited number of form fields and multipart parts.

The urlencoded parser splits the whole body on its separators at once, creating one scalar per separator before any field is stored. This costs about 90 bytes of memory per separator byte. The multipart parser creates a temporary file for every part that carries a filename. Neither parser limits how many fields or parts a body may hold.

A remote attacker can exhaust worker memory with a body made of separators, or create thousands of temporary files with one request of small file parts.

CVE-2026-118986.title: CallBackery versions before 0.62.0 for Perl allow session cookie forgery via a signing secret generated with rand()
CVE-2026-118986.description:
CallBackery versions before 0.62.0 for Perl allow session cookie forgery via a signing secret generated with rand().

The secret that signs session cookies is built from two calls to the built-in rand(), which is seeded with 32 bits. The secret therefore has at most 2**32 possible values, and one signed cookie is enough to test each candidate offline.

An attacker who obtains a single session cookie can recover the secret and sign cookies for any user, including an administrator.

CVE-2026-128084.title: sqlite3-ruby: SQL Query Truncation
CVE-2026-128084.description: sqlite3 provides Ruby bindings for the SQLite3 embedded database. Prior to 2.10.2, sqlite3-ruby casts Ruby string lengths to int before passing SQL through Database#prepare, bound String or Blob values through Statement#bind_param, and String or Blob results from Ruby-defined SQL functions and aggregates through Database#create_function and Database#create_aggregate. On 64-bit platforms, a string of 4 GiB (2^32 bytes) or larger can wrap the length so SQLite processes only a prefix. A truncated SQL string can drop trailing clauses such as a WHERE condition, while a truncated bound value matters only when the application validated the full value before binding it. Exploitation requires the application and server to accept and retain the unusually large attacker-controlled string. If a dropped SQL clause contained a bind placeholder, binding raises SQLite3::RangeException instead of running the query. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-131183.title: SPL Injection through Classic Dashboard in Splunk Enterprise
CVE-2026-131183.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands into a Classic Dashboard search. When another user opens the affected dashboard in Splunk Web, those injected commands execute with the viewing user's permissions, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to access stored credentials and write data to indexes.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape user-supplied content when it rewrites a search, which lets the rewritten search include additional SPL commands.
The vulnerability requires another user to open the dashboard in Splunk Web. Consequently, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see SPL safeguards for risky commands…

CVE-2026-63475.title: isomorphic-git: Circular symbolic references cause non-terminating resolution (DoS)
CVE-2026-63475.description: isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.6, isomorphic-git persists server-supplied circular symref= capabilities through updateRemoteRefs, and GitRefManager.resolve() follows the resulting loose symbolic references without a default depth limit or cycle detection. After a clone from a malicious or man-in-the-middle-controlled remote, operations such as log, status, checkout, and branch that resolve refs/remotes/origin/a or refs/remotes/origin/b do not terminate. The circular references remain on disk, leaving the repository unusable for the application and causing a persistent denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.6.

CVE-2026-65600.title: Traefik before v2.11.52 Authentication Bypass via ReplacePathRegex
CVE-2026-65600.description: Traefik versions <= v2.11.51, >= v3.6.0 <= v3.6.22, and >= v3.7.0 <= v3.7.6 contain an authentication bypass via path traversal in the ReplacePathRegex middleware. When ReplacePathRegex is configured with a regex that captures user-controlled path segments without a mandatory path separator (e.g. regex "^/api(.*)", replacement "/$1"), the middleware forwards the replaced path to the backend without validating that it matches its normalized form. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a crafted request (e.g. GET /api../admin) that produces an un-normalized path such as /../admin, which a backend that normalizes paths resolves to a protected route, bypassing authentication middleware. Fixed in v2.11.52, v3.6.23, and v3.7.7.

CVE-2026-99232.title: tracing/syscalls: Use copy_from_user for the faultable syscall buffer
CVE-2026-99232.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing/syscalls: Use copy_from_user for the faultable syscall buffer

syscall_copy_user_array() copies the buffer argument of faultable
syscalls (write, pwrite64, ...) with __copy_from_user(), which skips
access_ok(). Use copy_from_user() instead so a non-user address is
rejected and the entry is recorded as faulted.

It could be a security concern for machines that trust perf a bit too
much.
